name: Anti-nuclear movement
summary: The anti-nuclear movement opposes nuclear weapons and nuclear power. It holds that available nuclear weapons will eventually be used and seeks to rid the world of them, and that nuclear power is too dangerous, its accidents inevitable and its waste undisposable, favouring renewable energy instead. Beyond nuclear technology its defining sources state no doctrine on the economy, the state or society.

scope: The social movement against nuclear weapons and nuclear power as Britannica, the EBSCO Research Starters entry and Encyclopedia.com define it, . It excludes the positions of member organisations such as Greenpeace and the strands of the wider environmental or peace movements, and the entries say nothing on questions outside nuclear technology.

missingStatements.rationale: The entries present abolition of every nuclear weapon as the movement's goal.

quotes.text: Antinuclear activists generally believe that if nuclear weapons are available, these weapons will eventually be used; they therefore seek to rid the earth of all such armaments.

missingStatements.text: Nuclear power should be phased out.
missingStatements.rationale: The entries present opposition to nuclear power generation as part of the movement, many seeking a complete moratorium.

quotes.text: Many seek a complete moratorium on nuclear development and research.
Many members of the antinuclear movement are also against the development and expansion of nuclear power generation.

notes: Searched the defining entries (Britannica, EBSCO, Encyclopedia.com) for every theme; they speak only to nuclear weapons and nuclear power, so all other statements are null. Organisation platforms (Greenpeace, Abolition 2000) and Lovins's soft energy path were not used as coatracks. The second missing-statement quote for abolition is drawn from the Abolition 2000 passage in s2 that reports a convention for phasing out all nuclear weapons.
